thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT detected: hosted-api cluster - spike in 5xx (5m avg 7.8% -> 18.2%) https://incident.redwood.local/1769991111 :rotating_light:
ops-bot: Alert: PROD_HIGH_5XX_RATE firing (severity=page)

simon: Ack'ing — I'm oncall. Looking now. Any customer-facing outages?

maria: I'm seeing error graphs in the console, some customer requests returning 502s. A couple of enterprise tenants reported degraded responses.

jane: Adding context: we rolled a small runtime kernel patch ~30m ago to reduce mem usage. Might be related.

simon: Good call. Pulling pod logs and checking deploy history.

alex: Paging in case we need a quick rollback — I'm available.

ops-bot: Pager duty: simon is on call (primary). Handoff window ends in 40m.

simon: Quick live checklist:
- correlate deploys (kubectl get rs)
- check node GPU memory and OOMs
- tail logs for janky KV cache errors
- temporarily route new requests to fallback model variant if needed

elena: While you do that I can open a maintenance window in prometheus/alertmanager to stop repeated pages. Propose 30m silence for PROD_HIGH_5XX_RATE and related noisy alerts.

maria: +1 for a short silence, but only after we confirm mitigation so we don't mask real problems.

simon: Agreed. First attempt: scale up runtime pool by +2 nodes, enable fallback routing to model-v1-compat for latency-sensitive routes. Rolling back kernel patch if correlation points to deploy.

jane: Logs show a flood of "KVCache::miss escalate" starting right at 1769990900. Sample:
```
[2026-06-12T18:41:40Z] ERROR runtime: KVCache miss escalated for req=abcd1234 model=redwood-3b seq=128
[2026-06-12T18:41:41Z] WARN  runtime: fallback triggered for tenant=acme-corp
```

alex: I pushed a rollback to the runtime-amd64: rollback-20260612 tag. Kubernetes rollout started.

ops-bot: Deploy event: rollback-20260612 started by alex (link: https://deploys.redwood.local/rollback-20260612)

simon: I'm seeing error rate dropping after rollback and routing change. 5xx -> 6.1% in the last 5m and trending down.

elena: Initiating temporary silence in Alertmanager for the following alerts: PROD_HIGH_5XX_RATE, HOSTED_API_LATENCY_SPIKE, RUNTIME_KV_MISS_SPIKE. Duration 35m.

elena: Silence created: https://alertmanager.redwood.local/silences/si-176999 (expires in 35m) :white_check_mark:

maria: Can we also add a maintenance window for the hosted-api dashboards so we don't get noisy alert noise from synthetic checks?

devex-bot: Note: created maintenance window 'hosted-api-post-incident-176999' (window 35m) for synthetic checks.

jane: After rollback, we should tune the KV miss alert threshold. Current rule fires when miss rate > 5% for 2m — too sensitive for short bursts. Propose change to 10% for 5m and add a 'deploy-exempt' label so short deploys don't page.

simon: Sounds reasonable. Also add a low-priority notification route (email-only) for KV miss rule for 24h after deploys.

alex: I'll open a follow-up PR for alert rules. Draft snippet:
```
- alert: RUNTIME_KV_MISS_SPIKE
  expr: increase(runtime_kv_miss_total[5m]) / increase(runtime_requests_total[5m]) > 0.10
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
    team: eng-runtime
    deploy_exempt: "true"
```

maria: We should also create a dashboard panel that directly correlates deploys -> kv miss spike and surface which model variant is hit. That'll make postmortem faster.

elena: I'll add the dashboard tile and set default time range to 30m to capture short bursts.

simon: Post-incident action items (assignments):
- alex: finalize and merge alert rule PR + feature flag for deploy_exempt (due EOD)
- jane: add dashboard panel for deploy vs KV miss correlation (due tomorrow)
- elena: confirm silence + maintenance windows and export audit log (done)
- maria: run validation query to ensure new threshold reduces false positives (run after PR merged)

maria: Validation query (run in prometheus console):
```
sum(increase(runtime_kv_miss_total[30m])) by (job) / sum(increase(runtime_requests_total[30m])) by (job)
```

maria: Running now over past 7 days to see baseline — rolling 30m peaks show a median of 3.2% and 99th percentile 12.8%. The 10%/5m threshold should cut down noise but still catch real regressions.

alex: PR opened: https://git.redwood.local/eng-alerts/pulls/42 — includes tests and rollout plan.

jane: After merge, let's run the alert simulator to ensure we don't accidentally silence real customer-impacting regressions.

devex-bot: Alert simulation scheduled with 10 synthetic injections over next 24h. Report will be posted to #eng-runtime.

simon: Good work team. I'm marking this thread for the postmortem and tracking the follow-ups in the incident tracker. For now the customer impact window is 1769990800 -> 1769991200 (~6m effective impact for a subset of tenants).

elena: Exported audit: silence created by elena at 1769991120, maintenance window started 1769991125.

maria: I'll validate the new thresholds after PR merge and send a quick note to affected customers with timeline and mitigations.

ops-bot: INCIDENT resolved: error rate normalized below threshold and rollback confirmed. Incident ticket created: INC-2026-176999.

simon: Closing notes: we tolerated short noise with a targeted silence and maintenance window, avoided broad silences, and documented follow-ups. If anyone sees recurring pages re-open thread. :bow:
